title: Cinemas Once Hated Popcorn. What Changed?
parts: A century ago, cinemas did not want popcorn at all.
They wanted rugs on the floor, and no snacking.
Then the Great Depression closed cinemas by the thousands.
Just outside the doors, street vendors were already selling snacks to the crowds.
Owners got the message. Keep the ticket price low, and make your money at the stand.
One historian says popcorn really saved theaters during the Depression.
In the latest AMC and Cinemark reports, food and drink are about half or more of what is left after the studio's share and food costs.
The full story is in the video linked below.
